question: Within the certified finite Boolean universe, are semantic-equivalent transition-geometry differences fully explained by the declared structural-complexity covariates?
semantic_pair_definition: unordered pairs within each verified semantic class

components: AST maximum depth in edges from root
complexity_vector.orientation_rule: pairwise controls use componentwise absolute difference |z(G_i)-z(G_j)|, so unordered-pair results are not dependent on pair ordering

primary_geometry_measure.name: profile_hamming_divergence
primary_geometry_measure.definition: D_k(i,j) = number of universe destinations r for which R_k(G_i,G_r) != R_k(G_j,G_r)

secondary_geometry_measure.name: profile_l1_divergence
secondary_geometry_measure.definition: L_k(i,j) = sum over destinations r of |R_k(G_i,G_r)-R_k(G_j,G_r)|
secondary_geometry_measure.role: magnitude sensitivity check; it is not used to define the primary matched-stratum decision

exact_conditioning.within_stratum_test: Among semantic-equivalent pairs sharing an exact stratum key, check whether D_k is constant.
exact_conditioning.matched_definition: A semantic-equivalent pair is matched when its exact stratum contains at least two semantic-equivalent pairs.
exact_conditioning.nonconstant_definition: A semantic stratum is nonconstant for family k when its member pairs have more than one distinct D_k value.
exact_conditioning.claim_logic: If at least one exact semantic stratum is nonconstant, D_k is not a deterministic function of the declared pairwise complexity-difference vector alone within the semantic-equivalent pair set. This is the finite confound-exclusion result; it is not evidence for intrinsic geometry.

required_outputs_per_resistance_family: number of nonconstant matched semantic strata
number of matched pairs participating in nonconstant strata
minimum, maximum, and mean D_k among matched pairs
minimum, maximum, and mean profile L1 divergence among matched pairs

counts.N_eligible: all semantic-equivalent unordered pairs (expected finite universe count, not inferred from outcome)
counts.N_matched: eligible semantic-equivalent pairs in strata containing at least two semantic-equivalent pairs

analysis_order: construct z(G) for every syntax member
construct exact absolute pairwise complexity-difference strata
compute all three resistance-family full profiles
compute D_k and profile L1 divergence for every pair
restrict the primary within-stratum analysis to semantic-equivalent pairs
derive N_eligible, N_matched, N_separated and stratum diagnostics
interpret only after all calculations complete

interpretation.positive_control_exclusion: At least one nonconstant exact semantic stratum shows that the declared structural-complexity vector is insufficient to determine geometry-divergence magnitude even after exact conditioning within semantic-equivalent pairs.
interpretation.null: For a resistance family, D_k is constant within every semantic-equivalent exact complexity-difference stratum, so the tested complexity-difference control is sufficient to determine D_k within that restricted finite comparison.
interpretation.important_limit: A positive result does not show that semantic identity itself causes geometry differences, does not establish a deeper ontology, and does not establish intrinsic or uniquely correct geometry. It only excludes sufficiency of the declared pairwise structural-complexity control for the measured geometry-divergence quantity.
interpretation.sample_size_guard: Exact pair and stratum counts must be reported so any residual finding can be evaluated for breadth rather than inferred from a hidden or vanishing comparison set.

claim_ceiling: Within the certified finite universe and the preregistered resistance families, the assay can exclude or fail to exclude a declared structural-complexity explanation for the measured magnitude of outgoing-profile divergence. It cannot establish intrinsic representational geometry, semantic causality, future predictive value, behavioral consequences, temporal organization, or representation-space completeness.
